title: No world-writable files or directories
rationale: Useful deployed permission finding; scope traversal, unreadable paths and mount/symlink exclusions must remain visible.
criterion: No world-writable files or directories; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: env.php satisfies configured mode and ownership policy
rationale: 0640 and root owner/group are explicit defaults, not universal effective access policy; allow documented deployment ownership policy and explain ACL gap.
criterion: The collected app/etc/env.php Unix permission bits are a subset of configured mode 0640, and its owner and group match the configured reference paths (the project root by default). This is an explicit deployment ownership policy, not proof of effective ACL or web-process access restrictions.

title: Webroot hygiene (no .git/.env/backups in pub/)
rationale: Useful webroot leakage precursor; file absence is not runtime denial proof for aliases or alternate document roots.
criterion: Webroot hygiene (no .git/.env/backups in pub/); assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Directory listing absent on probed Magento paths
rationale: Keep bounded HTTP listing probes; show URLs tested and require runtime URL in LOCAL mode.
criterion: Successful responses from the configured runtime endpoint on /media/, /static/, /errors/ and /var/ must not expose recognizable directory-index markup. Scope is these paths at scan time; transport or unsupported responses are inconclusive.

title: Declared backend route differs from admin
rationale: Non-admin frontName is defense in depth; not proof admin is unexposed or authentication secure.
criterion: The collected app/etc/env.php backend.frontName declaration is a valid non-empty route and differs case-insensitively from admin. This assesses the configured backend route; route entropy and actual public reachability require separate evidence.

title: Admin 2FA core and provider modules declared enabled
rationale: Keep module declaration observation; cannot establish enrollment, provider health or bypass resistance.
criterion: In app/etc/config.php, the Magento_TwoFactorAuth module and at least one configured Magento admin 2FA provider module are declared enabled; this predicate assesses declared module state only.

title: Configured admin password minimum is at least eight
rationale: Eight-character configured admin minimum is basic policy only; label threshold explicitly and avoid ASVS-level inference. Missing from hardening.
criterion: The collected admin password minimum declaration, or the installed Magento User validator minimum when no declaration overrides it, is at least eight characters. This checks the observed admin policy, not every user password or ASVS conformance.

title: Configured admin login CAPTCHA or bounded lockout
rationale: Keep declared CAPTCHA or bounded lockout; demonstrate brute-force resistance separately and show chosen alternative.
criterion: Default-scope Magento admin login configuration enables native CAPTCHA for backend_login, recognized backend_login reCAPTCHA, or a positive lockout failure limit at most 10 with a positive lockout threshold. Locked env.php/config.php settings precede core_config_data. Custom authentication enforcement and runtime effectiveness require separate evidence.

title: Force HTTPS in admin and storefront
rationale: Entrypoint HTTPS redirects useful; require backend context to claim admin coverage and show all observed paths.
criterion: The observed HTTP storefront root and declared backend.frontName entrypoint redirect directly with 301/302/303/307/308 to same-host HTTPS. This is an entrypoint probe, not a universal guarantee for every deployment route.

title: Runtime endpoint rejects legacy TLS
rationale: Runtime TLS rejection useful; scanner capability/network gaps are UNKNOWN not server failures.
criterion: The assessed runtime host and port must accept TLS 1.2 or 1.3 and reject TLS 1.0 and 1.1. Rejection requires peer protocol-version alerts or successful active protocol enumeration; client-side protocol restrictions and connection failures are not proof.

title: Literal HTTP asset references absent in assessed markup/CSS
rationale: Literal HTTP references scoped to observed markup/CSS; runtime JS and authenticated routes remain untested.
criterion: In LOCAL mode, readable markup/CSS files under app must contain no literal HTTP subresource or form-action references. In REMOTE mode, successful HTTPS pages at configured paths must contain no literal HTTP subresource/form references. Dynamic code-generated URLs, external stylesheets and unvisited routes require separate assessment.

title: Sensitive cookies use Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite
rationale: Observed sensitive cookies only; configured anonymous paths do not establish authenticated admin cookie security. SameSite exclusions need app-specific review.
criterion: Sensitive session/admin cookies actually emitted by successful same-host HTTPS responses on the configured probe paths have exact Secure and HttpOnly attributes and SameSite=Lax or Strict. This assesses observed cookie emissions, not unobserved authenticated sessions.

title: Declared Magento deployment mode is production
rationale: Keep persisted production-mode declaration; do not market as live worker/runtime verification.
criterion: The collected app/etc/env.php MAGE_MODE declaration equals production. Runtime environment overrides and actual web process state require separate evidence.

title: Declared project debug settings are disabled
rationale: Persisted project debug declarations useful basic check; absent declarations only mean no explicit enablement, not live runtime safety. Missing from hardening.
criterion: Inspected default-scope project Magento debug/inline-translation declarations and project PHP ini display_errors/display_startup_errors and Xdebug declarations must not enable debug output. Absent declarations are not enabled declarations in this scope; web-worker runtime, custom integrations and all-component ASVS conformance are outside this predicate.

title: Published static artifacts present in assessed deployment
rationale: LOCAL one nonempty artifact and REMOTE observed CSS/JS are availability smoke checks; not theme/locale coverage or production completeness.
criterion: In LOCAL mode, pub/static/frontend or pub/static/adminhtml must contain at least one readable, nonempty published CSS/JS/font/image artifact. In REMOTE mode, same-origin Magento static CSS/JS assets referenced by the retrieved storefront must return nonempty non-HTML content with HTTP 200. This verifies observed deployment artifacts, not completeness of every theme, locale or route.

title: Declared Full Page Cache type enabled
rationale: LOCAL env.php full_page declaration and REMOTE cache-header heuristic assess different claims. Remote Via/Age/X-Cache can be CDN evidence; keep as separate signal, never claim persisted Magento FPC state.
criterion: The collected deployment app/etc/env.php declares cache_types.full_page enabled. This verifies the persisted Magento cache type state; Varnish selection and actual cache hit rates are separate observations.

title: Installed Magento cron entry present
rationale: Installed crontab entry is readiness only; entry presence does not establish job health or managed scheduler support.
criterion: At least one installed, syntactically valid cron entry invokes bin/magento cron:run for the collected deployment path. Sources include deployment-owner/current-user and configured-user crontabs plus /etc/crontab and /etc/cron.d. This verifies entry presence, not successful execution or an external orchestrator.

title: Composer dependency OSV advisory matches
rationale: Keep installed-version OSV advisory matches; expose source freshness, package coverage and unknown private packages.
criterion: Collected versioned Composer lock dependencies have no applicable OSV advisory matches in the successfully queried dataset, accounting for locally verified advisory-specific hotfix evidence. This does not certify absence of unknown vulnerabilities or uncollected runtime dependencies.

title: Adobe security release patch assessment
rationale: Keep Adobe patch evidence; explain version/edition and applied patch evidence, not merely latest release comparison.
criterion: The collected Composer-locked Magento product version is current for its Adobe security release branch according to the successfully queried patch dataset, or each required advisory patch is satisfied by verified local alternative evidence. Unsupported branches and missing required patches fail; this does not certify runtime patch deployment outside collected files.

title: No configured secret patterns in deployed application files
rationale: Useful deployed-file secret-pattern scan excluding runtime env.php and vendor; not universal credential absence. Missing from hardening.
criterion: Eligible deployed working-tree text files within configured paths and exclusions contain no configured secret-pattern matches. Git history is outside this basic deployment check. Runtime credential configuration app/etc/env.php is excluded; unreadable or oversized eligible files are collection errors.

criterion: Code directories are read-only for the application runtime in the collected Magento deployment; assess effective runtime identity, permissions, ACLs and read-only mounts.

rationale: Upload/source signals cannot prove server nonexecution; inspect serving config and authorized test. Identical media detector occurs twice, deduplicate observation while retaining obligations.

rationale: 900 seconds is an explicit session timeout policy; distinguish declared value from actual authenticated expiry.

title: Recorded Admin role assignments have relational integrity
rationale: Relational integrity of admin-role assignments is useful DB hygiene, not approval of least privilege; review ACL separately.
criterion: Collected admin_user, authorization_role and authorization_rule rows have valid user/group parent relationships, no cyclic group ancestry or orphan rules, and each active admin has one assigned group with ACL rules. This checks relational assignment integrity, not business approval, least privilege or effective authorization policy.

title: Global Admin ACL limited to approved roles
rationale: Global ACL needs customer-approved role roster, owner and exception review; keep DB signal but cannot infer authorization intent.
criterion: Global Admin ACL limited to approved roles; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

criterion: PCI vendor default account evidence assessment; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Database queries use safe construction and abstraction
rationale: Keep technical observations as review leads. Source-pattern presence/absence cannot establish complete behavior: trace trust boundary, effective framework controls and authorized positive/negative tests for this criterion.
criterion: Verify that data selection or database queries (e.g., SQL, HQL, NoSQL, Cypher) use parameterized queries, ORMs, entity frameworks, or are otherwise protected from SQL Injection and other database injection attacks. This is also relevant when writing stored procedures. No raw SQL without abstraction; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

rationale: Keep technical observations as review leads. Source-pattern presence/absence cannot establish complete behavior: trace trust boundary, effective framework controls and authorized positive/negative tests for this criterion.
criterion: Verify that output encoding for an HTTP response, HTML document, or XML document is relevant for the context required, such as encoding the relevant characters for HTML elements, HTML attributes, HTML comments, CSS, or HTTP header fields, to avoid changing the message or document structure. Verify that output encoding or escaping is used when dynamically building JavaScript content (including JSON), to avoid changing the message or document structure (to avoid JavaScript and JSON injection). Template output is escaped; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope. Escaping for JS context; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

criterion: Valid PHP files in the configured app subtree contain no T_VARIABLE references to $_GET, $_POST, $_REQUEST, $_COOKIE, $_FILES or $_SERVER. Comments and literal strings are ignored. This is a source coding policy, not proof of input validation.

Job success and scheduler retention are outside this criterion.

rationale: 1000 pending jobs is a capacity threshold, not universal security failure; evaluate age/group and deployment load.
criterion: The deployment cron_schedule table contains fewer than 1000 pending jobs whose scheduled_at is at or before scanner UTC time. Future scheduled jobs are excluded. This counts due pending scheduler jobs, not arbitrary application queues.

title: Dependency vulnerability remediation plan identifies an actionable resolution
rationale: Returned fixed version is remediation input, not actionable plan until owner, compatible upgrade/mitigation and deadline confirmed.

title: Enabled high-risk modules are maintained
rationale: Risk tagging identifies review candidates, not proof enabled high-risk modules are unmaintained; verify actual deployment inventory and vendor support.
criterion: Enabled high-risk modules are maintained; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

rationale: Mitigation documentation is evidence workflow; require affected risk, compensating control, owner, validation and expiry.
criterion: Temporary mitigations documented; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Known-exploited packages prioritized (CISA KEV)
rationale: KEV matches useful triage signal; human prioritization/workflow is separate. Show exact CVE-to-package linkage and applicability.
criterion: Known-exploited packages prioritized (CISA KEV); assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Collected transitive versions have no returned applicable advisories
rationale: Keep transitive advisory coverage; reuse advisory evidence with MB-0049, avoid duplicate customer remediation tasks.
criterion: No transitive package version in the complete collected Composer lock inventory is identified as affected by applicable advisories returned by the configured OSV service. Coverage is limited to the queried inventory and service data.

title: Declared constraints permit returned advisory fixed versions
rationale: Constraint ability to accept returned fixes is useful remediation readiness; require upgrade compatibility and dependency solver validation separately.
criterion: For returned applicable advisory findings with published fixed versions, the combined declared dependency constraints intersect versions at or above the published fixed version. This does not establish complete Composer solver feasibility, platform compatibility or every fixed branch.

title: Collected package versions are not reported withdrawn
rationale: Withdrawn version evidence is actionable supply-chain signal; missing package status must remain UNKNOWN.
criterion: Every package version in the complete collected Composer lock inventory has an explicit non-yanked status from the configured package-status source. Missing per-package status cannot establish a clean result.

rationale: Marketplace current/maintained is vendor-support readiness; latest version alone does not prove support or compatibility.
criterion: Marketplace extensions are current and maintained; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

rationale: Advisory publication age over30 days is not measured customer remediation SLA. Fresh critical advisory must still prioritize via MB-0049/0054.

title: Marketplace extensions have vendor support evidence
rationale: Vendor support requires authoritative entitlement/lifecycle evidence; source/API status alone cannot prove customer coverage.
criterion: Marketplace extensions have vendor support evidence; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Collected dependencies are not reported abandoned
rationale: Abandoned package status is maintenance risk not exploit proof; accept replacement/support exception with expiry.
criterion: No dependency package in the complete assessed Composer inventory is marked abandoned by the configured package-maintenance source; a clean conclusion requires explicit known status for every assessed package.

rationale: 24-month release recency can flag stable mature libraries; make configurable advisory rather than mandatory security gating.
criterion: For every versioned package in the complete collected Composer lock inventory, the configured package-status source reports known latest release history with a valid nonfuture latest release timestamp within the configured 24 calendar-month threshold. This is a maintenance policy, not proof of exploitability; unknown release history cannot establish a clean conclusion.

title: Reported source repositories remain available and active
rationale: Repository availability/activity is maintenance signal; archived upstream may have maintained fork, private mirror or support channel.
criterion: For every applicable source repository reported for packages in the complete collected Composer lock inventory, the configured package-status source explicitly reports that the repository is neither archived, disabled nor missing. Explicit repository-not-applicable classifications are outside scope; unsupported or unassessed providers cannot establish a clean conclusion. This is a maintenance policy, not proof of exploitability.

title: No risky forks replacing upstream libs
rationale: Fork risk needs provenance, patch delta, maintainers and support; not all forks are risky.
criterion: No risky forks replacing upstream libs; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: No wildcard constraints in composer.json
rationale: Wildcard constraint policy includes require-dev; lockfile pins deployment. Distinguish future resolution risk from installed vulnerability.
criterion: No wildcard constraints in composer.json; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: No dev branches in composer.json
rationale: Dev-branch prohibition includes require-dev; allow justified immutable commit pin and isolate production scope.
criterion: No dev branches in composer.json; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: prefer-stable=true in composer.json
rationale: prefer-stable=true is Composer selection preference; absence is not itself insecure when stability/lock choices already enforce stable packages.
criterion: prefer-stable=true in composer.json; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Direct locked versions match the reported latest stable release
rationale: Exact latest stable for direct packages includes dev and potential major upgrades; split upgrade hygiene from security-remediation urgency.
criterion: Collected direct Composer package versions are not older than the latest stable release reported by the configured package-status source. This is a maintenance policy, not proof of an exploitable vulnerability.

title: Composer lock hash and dependency identities are consistent
rationale: Lock hash/dependency identity consistency useful release integrity; not proof artifact provenance or installation exactness.
criterion: composer.lock has a matching Composer content-hash, no duplicate or malformed package identities, and contains or provides/replaces each declared root package dependency. This does not prove the full dependency solver result or installed vendor file integrity.

title: No configured secret-pattern matches in collected VCS scope
rationale: Git history needs source checkout. Deployed releases often omit .git; retain optional source-history check plus restore MB-0730 deployment secret scan in hardening.
criterion: No configured PCRE secret-pattern matches occur in eligible nonbinary working-tree files up to max_file_bytes and in individual file lines across available local Git ref history, within configured paths and exclusions. Git metadata and Git PCRE support are required for a clean history conclusion. This does not certify absence of every secret format, multiline historical matches, excluded files, remote refs or unavailable history.

title: HTTPS-only endpoints configured
rationale: Keep technical observations as review leads. Source-pattern presence/absence cannot establish complete behavior: trace trust boundary, effective framework controls and authorized positive/negative tests for this criterion.
criterion: HTTPS-only endpoints configured; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Webhook signature validation present
rationale: Keep technical observations as review leads. Source-pattern presence/absence cannot establish complete behavior: trace trust boundary, effective framework controls and authorized positive/negative tests for this criterion.
criterion: Webhook signature validation present; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Outbound connections restricted by allow-list
rationale: Network allowlist needs effective firewall/proxy policy and authorized egress testing; code patterns only support review.
criterion: Outbound connections restricted by allow-list; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: PII minimization for third-party flows
rationale: PII minimization requires purpose/data-flow inventory and payload evidence; absence of source patterns cannot prove minimization.
criterion: PII minimization for third-party flows; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Strong TLS ciphers on upstream gateways
rationale: Gateway cipher configuration file is not effective negotiated TLS across load balancers; require endpoint and runtime evidence.
criterion: Strong TLS ciphers on upstream gateways; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: API keys stored in env.php (not in DB/plain code)
rationale: API keys need protected secret management; env.php is one implementation, not universal correct storage. Assess encryption/access/exposure and approved external vaults rather than force env.php.
criterion: API keys stored in env.php (not in DB/plain code); assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: SaaS integrations scoped by ACL (least privilege/IP allowlist)
rationale: SaaS least privilege needs actual token scopes, tenant settings and network policy; code/config only supporting evidence.
criterion: SaaS integrations scoped by ACL (least privilege/IP allowlist); assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.
